standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness gives going down, hence dimension of the source localisation is at most that of the target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-dimension-going-up}, cited at proof lines 10839-10841

standard_prerequisites.name: An etale ring map is quasi-finite and a quasi-finite map has discrete fibres
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-etale-quasi-finite}, cited at proof lines 10847-10850
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the induced chain of primes in the source localisation strictly increasing, giving the second inequality.

core_obligations: Use flatness and going down to prove the inequality from the source dimension to the target dimension (proof lines 10838-10841).
Take a chain of primes in the target localisation and map it to primes of the source (proof lines 10842-10846).
Argue that no two consecutive primes in the image chain can be equal, using quasi-finiteness and discreteness of the fibres (proof lines 10847-10853).
Conclude the reverse inequality and hence equality (proof lines 10854-10855).
proof_roadmap: First inequality by flatness and going down (proof lines 10838-10841).
Second inequality by pushforward of chains and quasi-finiteness (proof lines 10842-10855).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an etale ring map preserves the dimension of the localisations at a prime and a prime above it. The proof establishes the two inequalities separately: flatness gives going down, hence the dimension of the source localisation is at most that of the target; and any chain of primes in the target localisation maps to a chain of primes in the source localisation, which is strictly increasing because an etale map is quasi-finite and a quasi-finite map has discrete fibres on spectra, giving the reverse inequality. Both inequalities are argued directly from the cited properties.
